top_stories.title: Cooling inflation but a wobbling consumer leave markets mixed
points: July CPI (Consumer Price Index, the main gauge of what households pay for goods and services) rose 3.4% year over year, down from June's 3.5% and in line with forecasts, driven mainly by shelter while energy prices fell.
Core CPI (the same index stripped of volatile food and energy) slowed to 2.5%, signaling underlying price pressures are moderating.
July PPI (Producer Price Index, wholesale prices charged by producers) was flat versus expectations of a small rise, with the annual rate cooling to 4.7% as goods fell and services gained.
The S&P 500 hit a fresh all-time high on the inflation data before fading; for the week the S&P rose 0.36%, the Nasdaq 0.14%, and the Dow slipped 0.56%.
Friday brought a pullback: consumer sentiment dropped sharply and July retail sales fell, sending the S&P 500 and Dow down 0.2% and the Nasdaq down 0.3%.
The dollar hit its lowest level since May as weak retail data shifted interest-rate expectations.

unique_angles.point: Energy was the week's standout sector, up 7.3%, as WTI crude (the U.S. benchmark oil price) jumped 5.4% to $82.40 a barrel.
Despite the losses, indices remain within striking distance of records and Wall Street's riskiest trades keep booming.

items.title: Storage and semiconductor stocks rip on AI demand
points: SanDisk surged 35%, Super Micro Computer 28%, Seagate 20% and Western Digital 17% on strong AI-related hardware demand.
Marvell Technology and DRAM-focused names (DRAM is the fast memory chips used in servers and PCs) gained on AI memory and storage optimism, with analysts flagging possible bullish reversals.

items.title: Trump commits $94.4M-plus to critical minerals
points: The administration announced $85M for bauxite (the ore aluminum is made from) supply-chain security, $1.4B for battery technology manufacturing and $8M for boron deposit development to cut China reliance.
The materials underpin EV production and advanced manufacturing, an awkward fit with Trump's public opposition to the EV sector.
Automakers and materials suppliers stand to benefit, but the policy contradiction adds uncertainty.

items.title: Earnings and analyst calls send mixed signals
points: Barrick Mining, Sea Limited, CoreWeave and Applied Materials reported, with focus on semiconductor and infrastructure plays.
Uber was upgraded on growth engines offsetting autonomous-vehicle (self-driving car) spending risk; Netflix was downgraded on subscription cannibalization and Lucid on cash burn.
Tapestry fell 21% as luxury struggled, alongside downgrades of Starwood Properties and Axsome Therapeutics.

items.title: Reddit joins the S&P 500 but faces an AI dilemma
points: Reddit's stock surged on news it enters the S&P 500 next week.
Ads make up over 90% of Reddit's revenue, and executives are debating how much AI data-licensing deals (selling user posts to train AI models) cannibalize that base.
Shares have fallen double digits year to date whenever new licensing announcements slowed, despite growing ad revenue and users.
Longer term, selling its content archive risks accelerating Reddit's own replacement and eroding its credibility as the 'heart of the internet' if AI-generated posts proliferate.

items.title: Robinhood co-founder pitches AI data centers in space
points: Baiju Bhatt proposes building power grids and AI data centers in orbit so they don't compete with terrestrial energy supply for people.
The idea reflects mounting environmental and logistical constraints on Earth-based data center expansion.
Yahoo separately notes even $1 trillion in cash can't fix AI buildout bottlenecks like power, land and semiconductor supply.

items.title: Deal activity: Bezos, Rinehart, Workday
points: A Jeff Bezos consortium acquired roughly a 30% stake in Liverpool FC, and Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital put $215 million into Amazon.
Mining tycoon Gina Rinehart revealed a $1.4 billion SpaceX stake; Workday jumped on acquisition talks with private equity firm Silver Lake.

items.title: Consumer and corporate odds and ends
points: Apple proposes taking a 15% cut of purchases made outside the App Store.
California Tesla owners have until Sept. 25 to claim settlement money.

Morning Brief: Reddit is joining the S&P 500, but still has a huge AI dilemma

headlines: Reddit joins S&P 500 next week, triggering stock surge, but company remains caught between monetizing AI data licensing deals and protecting its 90%+ ad revenue base.
U.S. consumer sentiment dropped sharply as inflation concerns persist; retail sales fell in July, sending S&P 500 and Dow down 0.2% and Nasdaq down 0.3% Friday.
Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt proposes building AI data centers in space rather than on Earth to address energy infrastructure strain from AI buildout.
Apple proposes taking 15% cut of purchases made outside App Store; Tesla owners in California have until Sept. 25 to claim settlement money.

sections.title: Reddit's AI Dilemma: Can It Serve Both Users and Machines?
points: Reddit positioned itself as authentic human-content source for AI model training through lucrative licensing deals, but now faces existential tension between two revenue strategies.
Ad revenue comprises over 90% of Reddit's income; executives intensely debate how much AI licensing deals might cannibalize the legacy advertising business that sustains the company.
Wall Street punished Reddit stock with double-digit declines year-to-date whenever new AI licensing announcements slowed, despite expanding ad revenue and growing user base.

Long-term risk: If Reddit sells its content archive to train AI, it may accelerate its own replacement and damage credibility as 'heart of the internet' by facilitating AI-generated content proliferation.

sections.title: Market Sentiment Weakens on Consumer Concerns
points: Consumer sentiment dropped Friday, reflected in hard data showing retail sales fell during July, triggering broader market pullback across major indices.
Despite recent losses, markets remain within striking distance of record highs, with Wall Street's riskiest trades continuing to boom.
Dollar hit lowest level since May as weak retail data dimmed expectations for interest rate decisions.

sections.title: Notable Deal Activity and Corporate Moves
points: Jeff Bezos consortium acquired roughly 30% stake in Liverpool FC; Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital invested $215 million in Amazon.
Mining tycoon Gina Rinehart revealed $1.4 billion SpaceX stake; Workday stock surged on acquisition talks with private equity firm Silver Lake.
AI infrastructure remains constrained: even $1 trillion in available cash cannot solve fundamental bottlenecks in the AI buildout (e.g., power, land, semiconductor supply).

sections.title: Space as AI Solution
points: Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt explicitly proposed building power grids and AI data centers in space to avoid competing with terrestrial energy infrastructure demands for people.
This reflects growing recognition that Earth-based data center expansion faces environmental and logistical constraints that make space-based infrastructure conceptually attractive.
The proposal indicates pressure from tech leaders to find alternatives as AI-driven electricity demand increasingly strains planetary resources.
